freeForever: We think the tools you need to look after yourself should not be locked behind ads or a paywall. VitaLibre has no ads, no subscription, no account and no locked features. Everything it can do is available the moment you open it, and it will stay that way. The donations on the Donate screen are entirely optional and unlock nothing. They exist only if you want to help pay for the work, and we are grateful if you do.
nothingSentTitle: Your readings stay under your control
nothingSent: VitaLibre processes camera images on your device and does not upload them or your readings to the developer. It has no account, analytics, advertising, or developer server. Readings are saved on your device; your operating system may include app data in device backups. Sharing a reading is your choice and uses the app you select. If you choose to support development, the App Store or Google Play handles the purchase and receives the information needed to process it. No health reading is sent with that payment.
disclaimer: Not a medical device, results provided are an estimate only.
regulatory: Not a medical device. Not FDA-cleared or CE-marked. Not intended to diagnose, treat, cure or prevent any disease or condition.
disclaimerBody: This app is for general wellness and information only. It does not diagnose, treat, cure or prevent any condition. Heart rate and blood pressure values are estimates, may be inaccurate, and have not been clinically validated. A blood pressure estimate that looks normal does not mean your blood pressure is normal, and a cuff reading always takes precedence over this app. Do not use these values to make medical decisions or to start, change or stop any treatment. Consult a qualified health professional for medical advice. If you think you may be having a medical emergency, contact your local emergency services.
calibrationHow:
Calibrate only when your blood pressure is typical for you: rested, calm and well. If it is not, wait. A calibration made when your pressure is unusual shifts every later reading until you reset it.

Choose one of two ways. Each has two steps, and both are done at rest.

A. With a fresh cuff reading
1. Rest for five minutes, then take a reading with a validated cuff.
2. Straight away, take a reading with the app, tap Calibrate and enter the cuff numbers.

B. With a known resting pressure
1. Under Calibration, enter your known resting pressure from an earlier cuff reading or a medical record, and tap Done.
2. While at rest, take a reading with the app straight away.

Reset in Calibration clears both.

Both ways: do them in the posture under Before you measure, with your arm supported at heart height. A cuff reading taken standing, talking or just after a walk is not a typical one.

On an iPhone only way A counts: blood pressure is shown while a paired cuff reading is recent. Way B only sets your starting point.
bpCaveat: Estimate only. A normal-looking figure does not rule out high blood pressure; a cuff reading takes precedence.
readingGuide:
Rest first. Sit quietly for 5 minutes, back supported, feet flat on the floor, legs uncrossed. No talking or scrolling. No caffeine, smoking or exercise for 30 minutes beforehand, and empty your bladder first.

Support your arm. Rest your forearm and hand on a table or a cushion at about heart height, and let the phone rest on that support. Don't hold it in the air, and don't press it against your chest: your breathing and heartbeat move it.

Place your finger. Cover the lens and flash completely with your fingertip, with light pressure. Pressing hard squeezes the blood out of the fingertip and weakens the pulse. Warm hands give a stronger signal.

If your hands shake. Rest your wrist and elbow, lay the phone flat and lay your finger on it. Shaking shows on the graph as stretches of low signal quality, which you can leave out of the result.

Keep it comparable. Measure at the same time of day, with the same hand and in the same position. When you calibrate, take the cuff reading in the same sitting, within a minute of the scan.
restTimerDone: Five minutes are up. Support your arm and start when you are ready.
